key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating delivered the best high-temperature oxidation resistance on SA516 steel by forming a dense, protective oxide scale and sharply reducing weight gain.
engineering_relevance: For boiler and other heat-exposed steel components, selecting HVOF Ni-Cr ceramic composite coatings can substantially improve oxidation life and reduce spalling-related degradation.
method: SA516 boiler steel was coated with Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN using HVOF and plasma spray.
Cyclic air oxidation testing was run for 50 cycles at 900°C.
XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping were used to assess phase evolution, oxidation products, and microstructure.
evidence_signal: The HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating reduced maximum weight gain by 95.71% relative to uncoated SA516 steel after cyclic oxidation at 900°C.
watch_item: Results are based on laboratory cyclic oxidation conditions, so real boiler service performance may differ under thermal gradients, corrosion species, and long-term exposure.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
